thread.title: New York investigates Apple iPhone glitch, calling it a 'serious threat'

author: Anthony Noto
title: New York investigates Apple iPhone glitch, calling it a 'serious threat'
text: – Reporter, New York Business Journal Jan 30, 2019, 7:51pm EST New York officials are investigating a recent Apple Inc. privacy breach. The joint probe , led by New York Attorney General Letitia James and Gov. Andrew Cuomo ’s office, will focus on what they say was Apple’s failure to warn consumers about a tech flaw that essentially turned iPhones into eavesdropping devices. Users of the FaceTime video-chat service were able to listen in on people they contacted even before the person accepted or rejected the call. Cuomo issued a prepared statement on the matter: In the wake of this egregious bug that put the privacy of New Yorkers at risk, I am calling on the attorney general to investigate this serious consumer rights issue. We need a full accounting of the facts to confirm businesses are abiding by New York consumer protection laws and to help make sure this type of privacy breach does not happen again. Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) listed FaceTime as temporarily unavailable on its site (see below). The company did not respond to a request for comment about James and Cuomo's investigation. “New Yorkers shouldn’t have to choose between their private communications and their privacy rights,” James said. “This FaceTime breach is a serious threat to the security and privacy of the millions of New Yorkers who have put their trust in Apple and its products over the years. My office will be conducting a thorough investigation into Apple’s response to the situation, and will evaluate the company’s actions in relation to the laws set forth by the State of New York. We must use every tool at our disposal to ensure that consumers are always protected.” According to CNN and The New York Times , the glitch was first discovered by 14-year old Grant Thompson . The teen's mother, an attorney in Tucson, Arizona, said she tried to get Apple's attention through email, phone calls, fax and Twitter — but to no avail. – Reporter, New York Business Journal Jan 30, 2019, 7:51pm EST Related Content
